blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Avoiding double taxation in practice is about knowing which relief mechanism applies to which income, and then claiming it correctly. Some treaties grant the primary right to tax to the country of source; others grant it to the country of residence. Some offer a full credit for the foreign tax paid; others offer only a deduction. Each difference can change the final tax by meaningful amounts.

The practical steps are three. First, identify the treaty that applies to the specific deal. Second, make sure the documentation needed to claim relief — certificates of tax residence, withholding statements — is in hand before payment, not after. Third, document the reasoning, so the same case can be explained to an auditor two years later without guessing.

If we were to ignore the treaty and pay the full tax in both countries, the deal would be significantly less attractive. Done correctly, most cross-border deals are competitive. Done carelessly, they become quietly expensive.

items.q: According to the text, what is avoiding double taxation mainly about?
options: Paying tax only in the country of residence
Avoiding cross-border deals altogether
Negotiating a lower tax rate with each government
Knowing which relief mechanism applies and claiming it correctly
items.why: "knowing which relief mechanism applies to which income, and then claiming it correctly."

items.q: When should the documentation to claim relief be in hand?
options: Before payment, not after
At any point before the audit
Only if an auditor asks for it
Two years after the deal closes
items.why: "is in hand before payment, not after."

items.q: Why does the text say to document the reasoning?
options: To reduce the amount of tax owed
To speed up the payment process
So the same case can be explained to an auditor later without guessing
To satisfy a legal requirement in every treaty
items.why: "so the same case can be explained to an auditor two years later without guessing."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Gathering documents early prevents problems later.
The choice of treaty can change the final tax meaningfully.
Cross-border deals are inherently uncompetitive because of tax.
A full credit and a deduction are not the same relief.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que, feitos corretamente, a maioria dos deals é competitiva — a desvantagem vem do descuido, não do imposto em si.

items.q: The phrase "they become quietly expensive" suggests that…
options: the tax authorities announce the extra charge loudly
the extra cost is obvious from the start
the deals are always cheap to run
carelessness raises costs in a way that is easy to miss
items.why: Inferência: "quietly" indica um custo que passa despercebido — resultado do descuido, não visível de imediato.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James orientando o novo gerente internacional. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so you have your first cross-border deal landing next week, and I want to walk you through how we keep it from being taxed twice. It is not complicated, but the order matters.

Start with the treaty. Pull the one that covers these two countries and read who gets the primary right to tax — source or residence. Do not assume it is the same as the last deal, because it rarely is. That single line changes whether we get a full credit or just a deduction.

Then, and this is where people slip, get the paperwork before we pay. The certificate of tax residence and the withholding statement have to be in hand before the money moves. Chasing them afterwards is a nightmare, and sometimes you simply cannot get them.

Last thing. Write down why you did what you did. In two years an auditor will ask, and I would much rather you point to a clear note than sit there guessing. Get those three right and the deal stays competitive. Get lazy on any of them and it quietly costs us margin.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does James say you should start with?
options: The treaty covering the two countries
The final tax calculation
The paperwork from the last deal
A call to the auditor
items.why: "Start with the treaty. Pull the one that covers these two countries."

items.q: Why does James warn against assuming the treaty is the same as last time?
options: Because the tax rate is always higher
Because who gets the primary right to tax rarely stays the same
Because treaties expire every year
Because the auditor changes each deal
items.why: "Do not assume it is the same as the last deal, because it rarely is."

items.q: What must be in hand before the money moves?
options: The certificate of tax residence and the withholding statement
The signed contract and invoice
The auditor's approval
The final tax return
items.why: "The certificate of tax residence and the withholding statement have to be in hand before the money moves."

items.q: Why does James stress writing down the reasoning?
options: Because an auditor will later ask, and a clear note beats guessing
Because the treaty legally requires a written note
Because the manager will forget the deal entirely
Because it lowers the tax owed
items.why: Inferência: "an auditor will ask… I would much rather you point to a clear note than sit there guessing."

items.q: How would you best describe James's overall message?
options: Auditors make cross-border deals impossible
The paperwork matters more than the treaty itself
Cross-border deals are too risky and should be avoided
Getting the three steps right keeps the deal competitive; slipping quietly costs margin
items.why: Inferência: ele resume que acertar os três passos mantém o deal competitivo e o descuido custa margem em silêncio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Each treaty offers a different relief mechanism for the same income." A relief mechanism is…
options: a type of cross-border contract
a penalty for late payment
a way of reducing or removing the tax burden
an official audit procedure
items.why: Relief mechanism = mecanismo de alívio, forma de reduzir ou eliminar o imposto.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The treaty gives the ___ to the country where the income is generated, not where the company is based."
options: certificate of tax residence
full credit
withholding statement
primary right to tax
items.why: Primary right to tax = direito primário de tributar, aqui atribuído ao país de origem da renda.

items.q: "We claimed a full credit for the tax already paid abroad." A full credit means…
options: the foreign tax is refunded in cash
the whole foreign tax can be offset against the domestic tax
only part of the foreign tax is deductible
no tax is due in either country
items.why: Full credit = crédito integral: todo o imposto pago no exterior é abatido do imposto devido internamente.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Before we release payment, we need the supplier's ___ to prove where it is taxed."
options: withholding statement
certificate of tax residence
relief mechanism
full credit
items.why: Certificate of tax residence = certificado de residência fiscal, prova de onde a empresa é tributada.

items.q: Country of source is best described as…
options: the country that signs the treaty first
the country where the company is legally based
the country with the lower tax rate
the country where the income is generated
items.why: Country of source = país de origem, onde a renda é gerada (em contraste com o país de residência).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre tributação e deals internacionais. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The tax director still has to sign off on the relief claim." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
reject outright
explain to the board
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We need to follow through and collect every certificate before payment." To follow through means to…
options: hand it to another team
cancel the plan
review it briefly
carry the task to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "The local office pushed back on our reading of the treaty." They…
options: approved it at once
rewrote the treaty
resisted or disagreed with it
ignored it completely
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Getting the paperwork after payment can hold up the whole claim." To hold up means to…
options: simplify
delay or block
approve
speed up
items.why: Hold up = atrasar ou travar o andamento de algo.

items.q: "Sorting out the treaty early really pays off at audit time." This means it…
options: must be repeated every year
produces a worthwhile benefit later
has no real effect
costs more than expected
items.why: Pay off = compensar, dar um retorno que vale o esforço.
